name: Seele
summary: AI game-studio agent that turns a text prompt, image or drawing into a playable 2D or 3D game in the browser, with Three.js, Unity and Unreal targets and generated 3D assets, images, video and audio, billed in Koin credits.
best_for: hobbyists, students and teachers who want to turn an idea, a drawing or a photo into a playable browser game without writing code, and indie developers who want to prototype a game idea quickly before building it properly
skip_if: you plan to sell or monetise the game on the $20 plan, because commercial use starts at Pro; or you need a fixed budget per project, because Koin costs are only known after the work; or you need guaranteed access to the source code, because the help centre says code download is not currently available
honest_knock:
You cannot know in advance what a game will cost. Koins are deducted by the AI time, cloud time and third-party tools a task uses, and the help centre says every change you ask for, from renaming a character to fixing a bug, is a new generation that costs Koins again. It also says Unity projects cost significantly more than lightweight Three.js web games. The 360 free Koins are meant for a first build, and one public review we read, from a 16-year-old, says he ran out before finishing his first game.

The cheapest plan does not let you sell what you make. Commercial use is listed on Pro and Ultra only, and the terms (section 4.2, updated 28 July 2026) say the right to publish, sell or advertise in your games comes with an active subscription at Pro or above, which is $100 a month or $78 billed annually (read on seeles.ai/upgrade on 17 November 2026 in our own test session). On Standard at $20 you can build and share, not earn.

The pricing page and the terms disagree on the two things that protect your money. The upgrade page FAQ says unused Koins roll over and the help centre says they never expire, while the terms say unused subscription Koins do not carry over to the next billing period. The upgrade page advertises a 7-day free trial and a 7-day money-back guarantee, while the terms say all payments are final and non-refundable, and that refunds may be refused for anything bought with a coupon or discount, which would cover the 50% first-month offer the page applied by default on 2 October 2026; we did not see that offer on 17 November. The terms also say a chargeback raised without first emailing support will be treated as fraud. Finally, the homepage promises you can take your Unity project with you, while the help centre's article on Koins says source code download is currently not available. We did not try to export a project ourselves.

The export picture has moved since we first read it. Seele's guide, read on 27 October 2026, tells you to switch to the files view to review, download or export the project, and lists Three.js, Unity, Godot and Unreal as target engines, with typical output ranging from a playable web build to a Unity project with a WebGL or mobile build. Its llms.txt draws the line for Unreal: the browser-playable 3D build is not a native Unreal project or .uproject, and Blueprint, C++, plugins and packaging must be built and validated separately. Seele's upgrade page, read on 17 November 2026 in our own test session, lists project downloads from Standard upward and not on the free plan, so do not count on one with the sign-up Koins.

The terms also contradict themselves on Koins. Section 5.3 says Koin does not expire and stays in your account until used; section 5.5 says unused subscription Koin does not carry over to the next billing period. The likely reading is that bought Koin Packs stay and the monthly plan allowance resets, but the terms do not say so in those words. On termination, unused Koin and subscription time are forfeited without refund. Disputes go to binding arbitration in Hong Kong, the minimum age is 13 (with parental consent under 18), and section 8.3 gives Seele a licence to use your games, screenshots and gameplay footage in its own marketing, next to a note that the AI may generate similar or identical output for other users.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read on seeles.ai/upgrade on 17 November 2026 in our own test session) Standard is $20 a month for 2,000 Koins, Pro $100 for 12,000 and Ultra $200 for 25,000; billed annually they show as $17, $78 and $167 a month. The Pro allowance is shown as 10,000 plus 2,000 Koins and Ultra as 20,000 plus 5,000. We read the monthly, annual and Koin Pack tabs in a browser. On 2 October 2026 the same page showed Pro at half that price with half the Koins, so Pro now costs twice as much for twice the Koins; Standard and Ultra are unchanged. Everything is paid for in Koins, the platform's credit, deducted per task according to the model, cloud time and third-party tools used, so there is no fixed price per game. A new account gets 360 Koins on sign-up, with no credit card. The toggle says annual saves 22%, which is true for Pro only; the plan cards themselves say 15% on Standard and 17% on Ultra. Standard unlocks full game generation, the Pro model and project downloads; Pro adds the Seele02-Ultra model and a commercial licence; Ultra adds all-channel commercial use including resale, 200GB of storage, a private cloud host, mini-game publishing and dedicated support. Koin Packs without a plan cost $20 for 2,000, $50 for 5,000, $200 for 20,000 and $500 for 50,000, and the pack page says bought Koins never expire. The plan cards say unused Koins roll over and never expire. On 2 October the upgrade page applied a 'New User 50% Off First Month' coupon by default; in our session on 17 November we saw no such offer on the plans. Payment by card through Stripe. The terms name SEELE AI, Inc. and the usage policy SEELE Technology Limited. Seele's llms.txt (read 27 October 2026) says a free tier is available and that commercial-use rights need an active Pro plan or above, and the terms (dated 28 July 2026) say prices are in US dollars and that a price change on a subscription takes effect at the next renewal.

compare_with.name: Rosebud AI
compare_with.why: Rosebud AI is the closest alternative: it also turns prompts into browser games and charges in credits. On its pricing page, read on 2 October 2026, Indie Dev is $15 a month, 10x Dev at $30 adds full commercial rights and removes Rosebud branding, Pro at $50 adds downloadable project code and Scale is $100; Rosebud says unused credits roll over once and then expire. So on Rosebud commercial rights cost $30 a month and code download is a listed feature at $50, while on Seele commercial use starts at Pro, $100 a month or $78 billed annually (read on seeles.ai/upgrade on 17 November 2026 in our own test session). Seele's upgrade page lists project downloads from Standard at $20, while a help-centre article we read in October said source code download was not available. Seele's case is breadth: Unity and Unreal targets, 3D assets, video and audio generation in the same workspace. Pick Rosebud if you want to own and sell a web game at the lowest price; pick Seele if you want a 3D or Unity project and a single tool for the game and its assets.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Seele in our free account: one prompt for a small cat game, which gave a game brief, 9 concept assets and a playable prototype in about 10 minutes for 45 Koins, the Pro badge on the button for the full game, the plans window on the Monthly and Annually tabs, and the cancel text in the FAQ. The full game, the checkout and the coupon were not reached. Nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at 16:21:53 (Dutch time) with a prompt sent at the workspace of the vendor site, in the free Seele our account (plan Free, 360 Koins), already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English. The model was Seele02-flash (Fast, affordable, perfect for basic games, Current); the Pro and Ultra models showed Unlock this model and were locked. The balance before was 360 Koins. Core action, a small game from one prompt: the prompt was A simple 2D game where a cat jumps over boxes; arrow keys to move, space to jump, score counter. After about 1 minute the app asked 3 questions: Engine (Three.js, Godot, Unity or Unreal, where Unreal was locked), Art style and Run length; we chose Three.js, Pixel arcade and Endless score chase (the recommended default), which took 5 extra clicks. Seele then made a Game brief (Concept, Full game not built yet), 9 concept assets (covers, three cats and three scenes) and a playable prototype, with the message Worked for 9m 34s. The result stood at the latest at 16:32:41, about 10 minutes after the start. The balance after was 315 Koins, so 45 Koins were used; the page Usage and Koin said 29 spent this month and 315 current balance. The prototype (TRY THE BOXES) says that the shapes are drawn in code, so the art is not final. We clicked Start and pressed Space: the cat jumped and the score rose (SCORE 11, BOXES 1 / 26, COMBO 1.1x); after that the screen said THE BOX WON. with a button RUN AGAIN. So the result is playable, but it is a prototype with shapes and not a finished game. The full game: the button Make the full game with AI carries a Pro badge and so does the line LET AI BUILD THE FULL GAME in the brief; the text says the full game is built to commercial quality, with upgraded visuals, levels and audio. We did NOT click it, so no second generation was made and the full game was not seen. On the plan card Standard says it unlocks full game generation, so the Pro badge on the button and the Standard card do not match; this stays an open point. A survey (how did you find us?) appeared and was closed without filling it in; the offer Rate SEELE +100 Koins was not used. Plans: the Upgrade button opened the window One subscription, from games to 3D. Monthly: Standard $20 / mo (Unlocks full game generation, the Pro model and project downloads; 2,000 Koins / mo), Pro $100 / mo (Most popular; Flagship model plus a commercial license, best value; 10,000 + 2,000 Koins / mo) and Ultra $200 / mo (20,000 + 5,000 Koins / mo with the choices 25k, 37.5k, 62.5k and 125k; All-channel commercial use and Mini-game publishing). Annually (Save 22%): Standard $17 / mo (billed $200 / year), Pro $78 / mo (crossed out $100, billed $936 / year) and Ultra $167 / mo (billed $2,000 / year). The card in the sidebar said Upgrade to Pro $100 / mo with 12,000 Koin a month. Koin packs: 2,000 for $20, 5,000 for $50, 20,000 for $200 and 50,000 for $500. Differences with the dossier: Pro is $100 a month and $78 a month billed annually, where the dossier has $50 and $39; Pro has 10,000 + 2,000 Koins a month, where the dossier has 6,000; Standard ($20 and $17) and Ultra ($200 and $167) agree; the dossier says about 120 to 140 Koins give a playable game on the Flash model, and we used 45 Koins for the brief and a playable prototype, which is not the full game; the dossier says the upgrade page applies a 50% first month coupon by default, and we saw no such offer on the plans window or in the sidebar. Checkout: NOT reached. The click on Subscribe to Standard was refused by the permission layer of the session, so we did not go on to the Stripe payment screen, and the coupon could not be checked there. Cancelling: the FAQ in the plans window says Cancel anytime from your billing settings and that paid plans stay active until the end of the current billing period (the text was cut off). The account is Free, so there was nothing to cancel. The account menu has Profile, Usage and Koin, API Keys, Affiliate program, Creator Center, Preferences, Terms and account (User Agreement, Privacy Policy, Subscription and refund policy), Feedback and Log out; no Delete account button was found in Profile or in Terms and account, and nothing was deleted. Not tested: the full game, publishing or sharing, revisions and their Koin cost, the Pro and Ultra models, commercial use, the Stripe checkout and the coupon, the claimed 120 to 140 Koins for a playable game, and cancelling. Clean up: the account and the test project (Cat Jumping Over Boxes Game) were left as they are, with 315 Koins. All our tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The result is a prototype drawn in code, the full game button has a Pro badge while the Standard card says it unlocks full game generation, the Pro plan costs twice the dossier amount, the 50% first month coupon was not seen, the Subscribe click was refused so the checkout was not reached, and no Delete account button was found.
